newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Best on Ground - Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: Best on Ground - Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
WHAT'S WRONG WITH THE MAGPIES? TONY'S NOT SHAW
Under the heading "Myths and "Realities", the round 14 AFL Football Record ran the following.
"The myth: a coach is only as good as his cattle. This saying is based on the notion that a football team is totally dependent on the quality of its players. It is a myth."
"The reality: a coach's performance can dramatically affect the performance of the players - as a team and as individuals."
What would Collingwood players, officials and supporters have made of coach Tony Shaw's comments immediately after the Magpies' eight point loss to Geelong at the MCG on Saturday.

"I'll do anything," Shaw told the media. "Any gurus out there who can say 'we'll turn this around and help an individual', we'll do it. We'll try anything if anyone out there has got any clues, please write to me, ring me or do something."
It is a startling admission from Shaw who, less than two months ago, was the Magpies' messiah.

Days after Collingwood thrashed the Western Bulldogs and assumed ladder leadership in mid May, he signed a new contract binding him to the club until season 2000. The Magpies have been winless since and have plummeted to 13th on the ladder.
If the Collingwood coaching staff has run out of ideas, what hope is there for the team? At any rate, Telstra and Australia Post will appreciate the extra business Shaw's request is sure to generate.
EAGLES STONED BY CROWS

West Coast coach Mick Malthouse won't quite be reaching for the panic button but he will be looking for answers to the Eagles' miserable form after their 75 point thrashing by Adelaide at Football Park on Friday night.
Malthouse forecast tough times ahead for his team after the Crows killed the game as a contest early, jumping the Eagles to lead by 56 points at half time.
"At the end of the day, it's not the worst the club's going to do," he said ruefully after the game.
The Western Bulldogs maintained their one game break on the pack and virtually assured themselves of a top four finish with a strong 36 point win over Carlton at Optus Oval on Saturday.
Carlton coach David Parkin endorsed the Bulldogs as a bona fide premiership chance and said he had not seen a more even and committed team in years.
Bulldog forward Chris Grant finished with 27 possessions and four goals, clearly outpointing star Carlton defender Michael Sexton.
HEATLEY IGNITES SAINTS
West Coast discard Jason Heatley booted nine goals in St Kilda's 54 point win over reigning premier North Melbourne at Waverley Park on Saturday.
The Saints started brilliantly with five goals to nothing in the opening term to shock the Roos who looked sluggish after their mud wrestle with Sydney the week before.
In his third game for the season after shoulder surgery, North skipper Wayne Carey is yet to play in a winning team.
Clearly, the heavy SCG also took its toll on the Swans who, in losing to Fremantle by 15 points at the WACA on Saturday night, have not beaten the Dockers in five attempts.
The Dockers started strongly and led by three goals before torrential rain flooded the ground and virtually drowned the Swans' victory chances.

Hawthorn veteran John Platten capped a memorable 250th game with a best afield display and a towering torpedo punt goal after the final siren to give the Hawks a 32 point win over Port Adelaide at Waverley Park on Sunday.
Port trailed by almost 12 goals in the second quarter but crept within 17 ponts early in the final quarter before a Daniel Chick goal steadied the Hawks.
Essendon moved to within a game of the top eight with a 63 point win over Melbourne at the MCG on Sunday.
After an even first half the Bombers pulled away kicking 10 goals to three in the second half. Bomber forward Matthew Lloyd starred with eight goals.
Brisbane could manage only an 18 point win over lowly Richmond at the Gabba on Sunday despite 18 extra scoring shots.
Lions' defender Chris Johnson will appear before the tribunal to answer an alleged misconduct charge for unduly interfering with umpire Tim Shearer in the first quarter.
*Andrew Bartram is a freelance sports writer who will be writing a regular AFL column for Reuters. Any feedback to cybercafe@ca.com.au.
